text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. - - - -

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has pledged that the party will pay special attention tocombating the emerging problem of drug addiction among secondary school students in Hanoi's inner city district of Ba Dinh.
-- The government of Vietnam has moved to clarify its laws relating to the abuse of illegal narcotics, including those covering the death penalty.
-- The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank have again pledged to further help Vietnam's Doi Moi (renovation) process by providing more money.
-- Global software giant Microsoft has launched a promotional campaign in Vietnam, appointing Thakral Brothers (Pte.) Ltd to distribute its software products. - - - -
-- A special committee was established by the government for socio-economic development in the country's highland area.

-- A huge trade gap was reported in Ho Chi Minh City in the first nine months of 1996. The report said a large number of delayed-payment imports of consumer goods was the reason behind stagnation in production.
-- Some 13 corruption cases, which brought losses of around $1.2 million, were uncovered in Ho Chi Minh City in the first nine months of this year. - - - -
-- Flooding in the Mekong Delta provinces of An Gian and Dong Thap has killed 18 children and three adults, inundated 200,000 houses and left 300,000 households in need of relief aid. - - - -

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told National Assembly deputies and voters in Hanoi's Ba Dinh district on Sunday that he wanted to narrow the wealth gap and eliminate poverty. He added that tighten control is needed to crack down on tax dodging.
-- About 400 students joined the Communist Party during the 1995-1996 school year. - - - -
